about: Hand-written rotation guides for the hunter's player pages (guides.py).

raid.plan: Beast Mastery in a raid shoots from range with its cat out: keep **Hunter's Mark** and **Serpent Sting** on the boss, spend the cooldown **Summon Hawk** shares with **Arcane Shot** as hawk, hawk, **Arcane Shot**, fire **Aimed Shot** whenever it is ready, and use **Bestial Wrath** and **Rapid Fire** as they come up. This is the official simulator's own rotation with hawks (its turret_hawk file; since 2026-11-20, when it beat ours by 2.1% on this build). In a 3-minute raid fight: **Aimed Shot** 23 casts, **Summon Hawk** 20, **Serpent Sting** 12, **Arcane Shot** 10, **Bestial Wrath** 2, **Rapid Fire** 1; **Auto Shot** 31% of the damage, the cat's and the hawks' swings 30% (one line in the record), **Aimed Shot** 14%, **Serpent Sting** 11%, the cat's Claw 5%, **Arcane Shot** 5%, the hawks' dives 3%.
why: **Hunter's Mark** and **Serpent Sting** come first, each cast only when it is missing from the boss: the mark lasts 2 minutes (2 casts a fight), the sting 15 seconds (12 casts, never refreshed early; 20% stronger with **Improved Stings**). The mark and **Aspect of the Hawk** go up before the pull; **Deadly Aspects** needs the aspect: each **Auto Shot** then has a 10% chance to speed your shots by 30% for 12 seconds.

**Summon Hawk** and **Arcane Shot** share one cooldown, spent in a fixed order: hawk, hawk, **Arcane Shot**, then again (20 hawks and 10 Arcane Shots a fight, a use about every 6 seconds). A hawk dives for 108 plus 5% of your ranged attack power, then attacks for 18 seconds; only 2 can be out, and one every 9 seconds keeps both out nearly all fight. **Unleashed Fury** and **Ferocity** work on the hawks as well as the cat.

**Aimed Shot** whenever it is ready: a 2-second cast on a 6-second cooldown, 23 casts a fight. **Multi-Shot** shares that cooldown and is switched off for a single target (the rotation's "Use Multi-Shot").

From 5 seconds in, the rotation uses every other cooldown as it comes ready: **Bestial Wrath** (+50% pet damage for 18 seconds) about 5 seconds in and 2 minutes later, **Rapid Fire** (40% faster attacks for 15 seconds) once, your on-use trinket (the page's sets carry Blackhand's Breadth) and a Major Mana Potion. **Intimidation** has no line: the build takes it only because **Bestial Wrath** requires it.

The cat takes a tenth of your attack power and your crit chance. **Ferocity** (+10% crit), **Frenzy** (30% faster attacks for 8 seconds after each crit), **Unleashed Fury** (+15% damage) and **Bestial Wrath** build on that, and **Focused Fire** adds 2% to you both while it is out. It attacks and uses Claw on its own; keep it on the boss.
caveats: Full raid: every raid buff and debuff, phase-1 gear, 3-minute fights. The list has no mana guard: on the simulator's training dummy (your own buffs only), the raid's mana buffs alone (Mana Spring Totem, Mana Tide Totem, Greater Blessing of Wisdom, Judgement of Wisdom) add 18% to this build's damage.

Keep the cat alive with **Mend Pet**: Forever pets take no stat buffs from players, and a dead cat takes **Bestial Wrath** and **Focused Fire** with it. In the simulator a pet keeps the attack power it took from you when called until it is dismissed (its authors' reading of combat logs), so call it after your buffs are up.

The pet and the hawks are the simulator's models, unmeasured at 60: since 2026-11-19 a faster pet's swing hits for less, so its damage a second stays the same (fitted to one level-30 combat log), and the hawks' attacks after the dive, which the game files do not describe, are fitted to combat logs.

Ranks: the list casts the trainer's top ranks, **Serpent Sting** rank 8 and **Aspect of the Hawk** rank 6 (ranks 9 and 7 are class books, not in Forever on the evidence there is; checked again when the raids open on 2026-12-09). For **Hunter's Mark** the simulator uses rank 3's +98 ranged attack power, as the client data it reads lists rank 4 lower; the beta tooltip (build 70753) reads rank 4 +143. Cast whichever rank your tooltip shows higher.

Moving: **Auto Shot** and **Aimed Shot** stop while you move; **Arcane Shot**, **Serpent Sting** and **Summon Hawk** are instant. Move right after an **Auto Shot** goes off, as the simulator's walk to its spot does ("Windup close", "Just shot").
diverge: Two or more targets close together: **Multi-Shot** in place of **Aimed Shot** (it hits 3 targets). For a pack, **Volley**: a 6-second channel with no cooldown.
In the last few seconds, skip the **Serpent Sting** recast: its damage comes over 15 seconds.
Inside 8 yards your shots and **Auto Shot** stop: step back out. **Summon Hawk** has no minimum range.
Short on mana: let **Aimed Shot** go first. In this build's full-raid numbers it does about 1,030 damage for 310 mana, **Arcane Shot** 810 for 190, **Serpent Sting** 1,600 for 230.

leveling.plan: Beast Mastery levels with the cat as the tank: it holds the mob while **Auto Shot**, **Serpent Sting** and **Aimed Shot** kill it from range. The build puts its first 31 points into the pet (**Deadly Aspects** from level 10, **Unleashed Fury** at 20, **Ferocity** at 25, **Bestial Wrath** at 40) and then adds Marksmanship's crit and cheaper shots. Your job is to keep the mob on the pet and to spend mana only where it shortens the fight.
why: Send the pet first, then **Hunter's Mark** and **Serpent Sting**. In the fight lab the cat Growls every 5 seconds and keeps the mob until your threat passes 130% of its own, so two cheap openers give it a head start; the lab casts the mark only while the mob has more than 30% of its health and the sting while it has more than 40%.

**Aimed Shot** (from level 20) is your only cooldown shot on a single mob, cast while the mob has more than 35% of its health: below that, **Auto Shot** and the pet finish the mob, which the fight lab's tuned rules (2026-11-15) measured slightly faster. The rules never cast **Multi-Shot** (it shares the cooldown) or **Arcane Shot**: their mana is worth more as fewer drinks between pulls. This build has no **Summon Hawk** point (the rules switch the hawk off as well).

The pet talents come first: **Deadly Aspects** (levels 10-14), **Unleashed Fury** (20-24), **Ferocity** (25-29) and **Bestial Discipline** (30-31, half your mana regeneration keeps running while you cast). In the fight lab's removal runs at 60 (seconds a kill costs without the talent) **Unleashed Fury** is worth about 1.0 second, **Bestial Discipline** about 0.9, **Efficiency** (46-50) about 0.8 and **Ferocity** about 0.7: the build's four most valuable talents. **Trueshot Aura** (56) is a buff you cast in Forever: keep it on.

**Rapid Fire** (26) at the start of a fight whenever it is ready (a 5-minute cooldown here: no **Rapid Killing**); **Intimidation** (34) and **Bestial Wrath** (40) likewise, the pet's stun and rage at the pull. **Bestial Wrath** has a 2-minute cooldown, so it goes on the first pull and then again every few pulls.

At 60 the pet is about a third of your damage (35% in the fight lab) and your shots most of the rest. The bow cannot fire within 8 yards: if the mob ends up next to you while the pet holds it, step back rather than melee.

**Mend Pet** when the pet drops below about a third while it holds the mob, and between fights below half. A dead pet costs a **Revive Pet** before the next pull and your **Focused Fire** bonus until then. Between fights the lab drinks below 15% of your mana and eats below 65% of your health: the tuned rules of 2026-11-15 drink this late, since fewer stops measured slightly faster. Whenever you sit down to drink or eat, do both while the other bar is not full: it costs no extra time (the tuned rules of 2026-11-17).
caveats: **Intimidation** is the point that opens **Bestial Wrath**: cast on its own it measured slightly slower in the fight lab (about 0.2 seconds a kill), and **Bestial Wrath** itself is worth about 0.2. **Endurance Training**, **Bestial Swiftness** and **Spirit Bond** measured nothing at 60 (a sturdier, faster, self-healing pet; the lab's pet rarely dies).

A mob that turns on you: **Feign Death** sends it back to the pet; while it is on cooldown, **Mongoose Bite** after a dodge, **Raptor Strike** and **Wing Clip** until the pet's Growl takes the mob back.
Several mobs at once: **Multi-Shot** and **Volley** (from level 40; a 6-second channel with no cooldown in Forever) are your area damage.
**Improved Tracking** (levels 57-59, 3 points) adds 1% a point, and only against the creature type you are tracking: switch tracking to what you are killing.

Buy the new ranks: in the beta client (build 70753) the top ranks are the strongest. **Aspect of the Hawk** rank 7 gives +120 ranged attack power (rank 6 +110), **Hunter's Mark** rank 4 +143 (rank 3 +98) and **Trueshot Aura** rank 5 +100 (rank 4 +75). Cast the highest rank you know; the fight lab does.
**Auto Shot** keeps firing while you cast **Aimed Shot**, but after you step back it waits until you have stood still for half a second (Blizzard's 16 Oct notes), so don't shuffle between shots.
diverge: When the mob is nearly dead, stop spending mana: **Auto Shot** and the pet finish it, and you start the next pull fuller.
If the pet dies mid-fight, finish the mob with **Raptor Strike** and **Wing Clip** (or **Feign Death** if it is going badly), and revive the pet before the next pull.

raid.plan: Lone Wolf Marksmanship raids with no pet out: keep **Hunter's Mark** and **Serpent Sting** on the boss, then fire **Arcane Shot**, **Aimed Shot** and **Sniper Shot**, in that order, whenever one is ready. This is the official simulator's own turret rotation (since 2026-11-20; on this build it ties ours, +0.02%, and leads by 0.1-1.7% for the entry's other builds). In a 3-minute raid fight: **Arcane Shot** 37 casts, **Aimed Shot** 19, **Serpent Sting** 12, **Sniper Shot** 10, **Rapid Fire** 1; **Auto Shot** 39% of the damage, **Arcane Shot** 22%, **Aimed Shot** 17%, **Serpent Sting** 14%, **Sniper Shot** 9%.
why: Setup: **Dismiss Pet** (a 5-second cast), since **Lone Wolf**'s 20% to all your attacks counts only with no pet out. Cast **Trueshot Aura** too: in Forever a 30-minute buff (rank 5: +100 ranged attack power to your party and raid within 45 yards), which the simulator applies for you, so it has no line.

The opener: **Hunter's Mark** and **Aspect of the Hawk** 22 and 20 seconds before the pull, then **Sniper Shot** started 4 seconds before so it lands as the fight begins. The aspect is what **Deadly Aspects** needs: each **Auto Shot** has a 10% chance to speed your shots by 30% for 12 seconds.

**Hunter's Mark** and **Serpent Sting** whenever missing from the boss: the mark lasts 2 minutes, the sting 15 seconds (12 casts, recast as it falls off; 20% stronger with **Improved Stings**). Each sting starts **Rapid Recuperation**: half your mana regeneration keeps going while you cast for 15 seconds.
**Arcane Shot** whenever it is ready: **Improved Arcane Shot** brings its cooldown to 4.5 seconds, 37 casts a fight, the most of any button.
**Aimed Shot** next: +350 to a shot, 15% more with **Barrage**, a 2-second cast on a 6-second cooldown. **Multi-Shot** shares that cooldown and is switched off for a single target ("Use Multi-Shot").

**Sniper Shot** last: ranged damage plus 590 on a 4-second cast and a 15-second cooldown. The rotation's own note calls it the least damage per second of casting, so it waits until neither shot above is ready.

From 5 seconds in, every other cooldown as it comes ready: **Rapid Fire** (40% faster attacks for 15 seconds) once, your on-use trinket (the page's sets carry Blackhand's Breadth) and a Major Mana Potion. **Rapid Killing** cuts **Rapid Fire** to 3 minutes, a second one only past 3 minutes 5 seconds; the build takes it because **Rapid Recuperation** requires it.
caveats: Full raid: every raid buff and debuff, phase-1 gear, 3-minute fights. The list has no mana guard: on the simulator's training dummy (your own buffs only), the raid's mana buffs alone (Mana Spring Totem, Mana Tide Totem, Greater Blessing of Wisdom, Judgement of Wisdom) add 32% to this build's damage. **Efficiency** makes your shots and stings 9% cheaper.

Moving: **Auto Shot**, **Aimed Shot** and **Sniper Shot** need you to stand still; **Arcane Shot** and **Serpent Sting** are instant. Do not start a 4-second **Sniper Shot** when you must move soon; move right after an **Auto Shot** goes off, as the simulator's walk to its spot does ("Windup close", "Just shot").

Track the boss's creature type: **Improved Tracking** adds 5% only against the tracked type, and a Mechanical boss has none to track. The simulator's boss is an Elemental, so its numbers carry the full 5%.
**Rapid Killing**'s other half (a kill makes your next Shot within 20 seconds hit 20% harder) never happens on a boss; on trash, let the next pull's first **Aimed Shot** spend it.

Ranks: the list casts the trainer's top ranks, **Serpent Sting** rank 8 and **Aspect of the Hawk** rank 6 (ranks 9 and 7 are class books, not in Forever on the evidence there is; checked again when the raids open on 2026-12-09). For **Hunter's Mark** the simulator uses rank 3's +98 ranged attack power, as the client data it reads lists rank 4 lower; the beta tooltip (build 70753) reads rank 4 +143. Cast whichever rank your tooltip shows higher.
diverge: Two or three targets close together: **Multi-Shot** in place of **Aimed Shot** (it hits 3 targets). For a pack, **Volley**: a 6-second channel with no cooldown.
In the last seconds, skip the **Serpent Sting** recast and do not start a **Sniper Shot** that will not land before the boss dies.

With a pet instead: the page's With a pet setup (7/39/5: Focused Fire in place of **Lone Wolf** and a point of **Efficiency**) plays these shots with a cat out, 981 DPS in a full raid against this build's 996. Its entry runs the official turret file with our search's edits of 2026-11-20; with no **Summon Hawk** talent, the only one that acts for it is a Major Mana Potion line at the end (two potions a fight, not one), and on the official file it does 973.5.

Short on mana: let **Sniper Shot** go first. In this build's full-raid numbers it does about 1,670 damage for 365 mana, **Aimed Shot** 1,540 for 310, **Arcane Shot** 1,060 for 190, **Serpent Sting** 2,050 for 230.

leveling.plan: Marksmanship levels with the pet tanking, but more of the damage is your own: **Aimed Shot** on its cooldown, **Serpent Sting** on every mob, **Arcane Shot** to finish once the mob is below 35% of its health, **Trueshot Aura** always on and **Auto Shot** in between. The build spends its first 30 points on Marksmanship (**Lethal Attacks**, **Careful Aim**, **Efficiency**) and the other 21 on the pet.
why: Send the pet first, then **Hunter's Mark** and **Serpent Sting** while the mob is healthy (the fight lab: above 30% and 40% of its health). The cat holds the mob until your threat passes 130% of its own.

**Aimed Shot** gets the cooldown it shares with **Multi-Shot**, while the mob has more than a quarter of its health. The tuned rules (2026-11-03) never cast **Multi-Shot** on a single mob, and cast **Arcane Shot** only once the mob is below 35% of its health: earlier, its mana did less than the next **Aimed Shot** and **Serpent Sting**. In the band between a quarter and 35% of the mob's health both are allowed, and there the fight lab fires **Arcane Shot** before **Aimed Shot**, as the list above puts it.

**Lethal Attacks** and **Careful Aim** (levels 10-19) first, **Improved Stings** (20-22), then **Rapid Killing** (23-24), which cuts **Rapid Fire** to 3 minutes. **Trueshot Aura** (25) is a buff you cast in Forever: keep it on. **Efficiency** (26-29 and 31) is the build's most valuable talent at 60: about a second a kill in the fight lab's removal runs, ahead of **Unleashed Fury** (50-54, 0.9) and **Lethal Attacks** (0.7).

From level 40 the points go to the pet: **Deadly Aspects**, **Focused Fire**, **Endurance Training**, then **Unleashed Fury** and **Ferocity** (50-59), and the last point to **Improved Tracking** (60; its first at 39).
Your shots and stings are 71% of the damage at 60 in the fight lab, the cat most of the rest. **Auto Shot** cannot fire within 8 yards: step back out rather than melee while the pet holds the mob.

Drink below 15% mana rather than at 35%: it measured slightly faster (under 1% per kill). Whenever you sit down to drink or eat, do both while the other bar is not full: it costs no extra time (the tuned rules of 2026-11-17). **Feign Death** only while the mob has more than 35% of its health; below that, finish it.
caveats: **Rapid Recuperation** (30, one point; it needs both points of **Rapid Killing**): **Serpent Sting** lets a quarter of your mana regeneration continue while casting for 15 seconds, half after you spend a **Rapid Killing**. It measured about 0.4 seconds a kill at 60. **Barrage** (32-34) adds 15% to **Aimed Shot**, **Multi-Shot** and **Volley**: little on one mob (0.15 seconds), more on several.

**Rapid Killing** also makes your next Shot within 20 seconds of a kill hit 20% harder; the fight lab leaves that half out, so let the next pull's first **Aimed Shot** spend it. Without the bonus the talent measured almost nothing: its points open **Rapid Recuperation**.

**Endurance Training** (47) and **Improved Aspect of the Monkey** (48-49) measured nothing at 60 in the fight lab: they fill tiers. **Ranged Weapon Specialization** (35-38) is 4% more damage with your bow, and **Improved Tracking** (39 and 60) adds 1% a point, only against the creature type you are tracking: switch tracking to what you are killing.

A mob that turns on you while it still has more than 35% of its health: **Feign Death** sends it back to the pet; while it is on cooldown, **Mongoose Bite** after a dodge, **Raptor Strike** and **Wing Clip**.

Buy the new ranks: in the beta client (build 70753) the top ranks are the strongest. **Aspect of the Hawk** rank 7 gives +120 ranged attack power (rank 6 +110), **Hunter's Mark** rank 4 +143 (rank 3 +98) and **Trueshot Aura** rank 5 +100 (rank 4 +75). Cast the highest rank you know; the fight lab does.
**Auto Shot** keeps firing while you cast **Aimed Shot**, but after you step back it waits until you have stood still for half a second (Blizzard's 16 Oct notes), so don't shuffle between shots.
diverge: Several mobs: **Multi-Shot** and **Volley** (no cooldown in Forever) instead of single-target shots.
A mob on you while the pet is down: slow it with **Wing Clip** or **Concussive Shot**, step back past 8 yards and shoot.

raid.plan: Raid Survival fights in melee with two one-handers and a Raptor out: **Raptor Strike** whenever it is ready, **Hunter's Mark** kept up for **Expose Prey**, **Mongoose Bite** each time it lights up, **Strider Kick**, **Immolation Trap** and **Summon Hawk** on cooldown and **Wing Clip** in every global cooldown left, stepping out for **Serpent Sting** when it falls off. This is the official simulator's own melee rotation, build and pet (since the evening of 2026-11-20, when it beat ours by 4.1% on this build). In a 3-minute raid fight: **Wing Clip** 35 casts, **Raptor Strike** 24, **Summon Hawk** 22, **Mongoose Bite** 20, **Strider Kick** 20, **Immolation Trap** 10, **Serpent Sting** 9; the Raptor's and the hawks' swings 23% of the damage (one line in the record), your white swings 23%, **Immolation Trap** 7%, **Serpent Sting** 7%, Windfury Totem's extra swings 7%, **Raptor Strike** 7%, **Mongoose Bite** 6%, **Strider Kick** 5%.
why: Before the pull: **Hunter's Mark** and **Aspect of the Beast** (+110 melee attack power; with **Deadly Aspects** each melee auto attack has a 10% chance to speed your swings by 30% for 12 seconds). The simulator starts you 25 yards out and walks you in, casting **Serpent Sting**, **Arcane Shot** and **Multi-Shot** on the way. From 5 seconds in the other cooldowns go as they come ready: **Rapid Fire** (in Forever 40% faster melee attacks too, for 15 seconds) once, your on-use trinket (the page's sets carry Blackhand's Breadth) and a Major Mana Potion.
**Raptor Strike** first: it replaces your next main-hand swing and costs no global cooldown, so queue it whenever its 6-second cooldown ends.

**Hunter's Mark** whenever it is missing: with **Expose Prey**, each of your hits on a marked target has a 10% chance to light up **Mongoose Bite** for 10 seconds, and in a raid the boss hits your tank, so your own dodges, the bite's other trigger, rarely come. Bite at once (weapon damage plus 57, 5-second cooldown); **Lacerating Strikes** adds a bleed of 40% of it over 21 seconds (1.3% of your damage), which the next bite replaces, as in game.

**Strider Kick** on cooldown (full weapon damage, 8 seconds), and its 3 seconds of 30% speed are your window for **Serpent Sting**: with the sting off the boss and more than 30% mana, run out past your shots' 8-yard minimum range (the simulator goes to about 13 yards), sting, shoot **Arcane Shot** and **Multi-Shot** if they are ready, and walk back in, pausing for an **Auto Shot** when one is due.
**Immolation Trap** whenever it is ready, set in melee at the boss: 690 Fire damage over 15 seconds, 30% more with **Clever Traps**, every 18 seconds with **Survivalist's Discipline**.

**Summon Hawk** next: a dive, then a hawk that attacks for 18 seconds, two at a time, 15% harder with **Unleashed Fury**. It shares its cooldown with **Arcane Shot**, which the list casts only from range.
**Wing Clip** fills every global cooldown left: its own hit is 50 damage, but each hit on your marked target is another 10% chance at **Mongoose Bite**.
The Raptor is the simulator's own choice (Faster Attack II, a 1.6-second swing); its Claw is 4% of your damage, and **Focused Fire** adds 2% to you both while it is out.
caveats: Full raid: every raid buff and debuff, phase-1 gear, 3-minute fights. Windfury Totem's extra swings are 7% of your damage: you need a shaman's totem in your group.

Mana: no **Resourcefulness** or **Efficiency** in this build. On the simulator's training dummy (your own buffs only), the raid's mana buffs alone (Mana Spring Totem, Mana Tide Totem, Greater Blessing of Wisdom, Judgement of Wisdom) add 31% to its damage, and in a full raid it still drinks a Major Mana Potion a fight.
The class page says **Expose Prey** needs your own **Hunter's Mark**; the simulator accepts any hunter's. With several hunters, make sure the mark on the boss is yours.
Traps in combat are the simulator's assumption, still to check in game: a trap lies where you stand and springs on the boss beside you, so the list sets it only in melee.
Keep the Raptor alive with **Mend Pet**: Forever pets take no stat buffs from players. The hawks' attacks after the dive are the simulator's fit to combat logs.
Ranks: **Serpent Sting** rank 8 (rank 9 is a class book, not in Forever on the evidence there is, 2026-11-20) and **Aspect of the Beast** rank 4.
diverge: Adds around you: **Multi-Shot** on the way in hits 3 targets, and for a pack set **Explosive Trap** instead of **Immolation Trap** (everything within 10 yards). The official list never casts it, and the simulator gives all traps one cooldown, so it is one or the other.
When you must leave the boss, make **Strider Kick** your last hit: 30% movement speed for 3 seconds.
If you pull threat, **Feign Death** (30-second cooldown).

Short on mana: the list already skips the **Serpent Sting** trips below 30%; let **Wing Clip** go next, about 70 damage for 80 mana in this build's full-raid numbers, the least for its mana of anything you press.

leveling.plan: Melee Survival levels with the pet as the tank: you walk in behind it and fight beside it with two one-handers. **Raptor Strike** finishes the mob (with **Strider Kick** from level 54), **Mongoose Bite** comes when it lights up, **Immolation Trap** burns the longer fights, **Lacerate** adds a bleed from level 30, and white swings do the rest. The build puts 32 points into Survival, 18 into Marksmanship (**Lethal Attacks**, **Careful Aim**, **Improved Stings**, **Efficiency**, **Trueshot Aura**) and 1 into **Deadly Aspects**.
why: **Serpent Sting** as the mob comes in: the lab casts it from range, while the mob is still 8 yards or more away and has more than 40% of its health, then you walk in behind the pet. The tuned rules (2026-11-03) never cast **Hunter's Mark** for a melee hunter: it measured slower even with **Expose Prey**, the mark's only use for one, and this build does not take **Expose Prey**.

**Raptor Strike** is kept for the finish: the tuned rules cast it only once the mob is below 20% of its health. It replaces your next main-hand swing and costs no global cooldown, so queue it first when it is up. Held back, its mana buys more in the sting, the trap and **Lacerate**.

**Immolation Trap** goes at your feet beside the mob (traps work in combat in Forever but land where you stand), while the mob has more than 40% of its health (the burn lasts 15 seconds). **Resourcefulness** (levels 30 and 32) cuts the cost of traps and melee abilities by 60%.
**Lacerate** (trained at 30) only while the mob has more than half its health and you have 80% of your mana or more: cast freely, its mana cost more time than its bleed saved.

**Mongoose Bite** lights up after you dodge, so **Aspect of the Monkey** (its dodges) until level 30; then **Aspect of the Beast**: melee attack power, and with **Deadly Aspects** (50) a chance per melee auto attack for 30% faster swings for 12 seconds. **Deflection** raises your parry.

In the fight lab's removal runs at 60 (seconds a kill costs without the talent), **Resourcefulness** is worth about 2.5 seconds, **Survivalist's Discipline** (33-34, the trap every 18 seconds) 0.6, **Lethal Attacks** and **Surefooted** 0.5 each, **Efficiency** and **Clever Traps** 0.3 each: the build's most valuable talents. Melee, Raptor Strike, Mongoose Bite, Lacerate, Wing Clip and the pet are 53% of the damage at 60.

Between fights the lab drinks below 35% of your mana and eats below 65% of your health: the tuned rules change neither. Whenever you sit down to drink or eat, do both while the other bar is not full: it costs no extra time (the tuned rules of 2026-11-17).
caveats: This build does not take **Counterattack**, nor **Deterrence**, so the list above leaves their lines out; **Mongoose Bite** still goes whenever a dodge lights it up. **Strider Kick** (54), a weapon hit on an 8-second cooldown, has no line in the list: the tuned rules cast it like **Raptor Strike**, only once the mob is below 20% of its health. **Survival Tactics** (31) adds 5% to the chance your traps and **Feign Death** hit.
The pet is still your tank: **Mend Pet** below about a third in the fight and below half between fights, and let it build threat before you hit hard.

The project counts a melee hunter's damage as swings, strikes, bleeds and the pet (the spec's rule: at least half at 60; this build reaches 53%). The sting and the trap are not counted, which is why the rotation does not lean on them harder.
**Improved Tracking** (levels 10-14) adds 1% a point, and only against the creature type you are tracking: switch tracking to what you are killing.

The last points go to a second **Deflection** (51), a third **Improved Stings** (52), **Efficiency** (53 and 55-57), **Careful Aim**'s last two points (58-59) and **Trueshot Aura** (60). The leveling filler pass of 2026-11-17 took them from points the fight lab measured at nothing (Endurance Training, a fifth **Efficiency**, a second **Deadly Aspects**): the third **Improved Stings** measured 0.2% faster per kill, the others cost nothing.

Buy the new ranks: in the beta client (build 70753) the top ranks are the strongest. **Aspect of the Beast** rank 4 gives +110 melee attack power at 60 (rank 3 +90); the other ranks of the spells you press only add damage. Cast the highest rank you know; the fight lab does.
diverge: Two or more mobs: **Explosive Trap** instead of **Immolation Trap**; it hits everything within 10 yards and shares the fire-trap cooldown.
If the pet dies mid-fight, finish the mob and step back, or **Feign Death** if it is going badly; revive the pet before the next pull.

raid.plan: Beast-Marks puts Beast Mastery's pet talents on a Marksmanship shot core and plays the Beast Mastery list exactly, without **Bestial Wrath**: keep **Hunter's Mark** and **Serpent Sting** on the boss, spend the cooldown **Summon Hawk** shares with **Arcane Shot** as hawk, hawk, **Arcane Shot**, and fire **Aimed Shot** whenever it is ready. This is the official simulator's own rotation with hawks (its turret_hawk file; since 2026-11-20, when it beat ours by 2.1% on this build). In a 3-minute raid fight: **Aimed Shot** 23 casts, **Summon Hawk** 20, **Serpent Sting** 12, **Arcane Shot** 10, **Rapid Fire** 1; **Auto Shot** 32% of the damage, the cat's and the hawks' swings 28% (one line in the record), **Aimed Shot** 15%, **Serpent Sting** 12%, the cat's Claw 5%, **Arcane Shot** 5%, the hawks' dives 3%. In the same raid it does 942 DPS, against 946 for the Beast Mastery page's build.
why: **Hunter's Mark** and **Serpent Sting** come first, each cast only when it is missing from the boss: the mark lasts 2 minutes (2 casts a fight), the sting 15 seconds (12 casts, never refreshed early; 20% stronger with **Improved Stings**). The mark and **Aspect of the Hawk** go up before the pull; **Deadly Aspects** needs the aspect: each **Auto Shot** then has a 10% chance to speed your shots by 30% for 12 seconds.

**Summon Hawk** and **Arcane Shot** share one cooldown, spent in a fixed order: hawk, hawk, **Arcane Shot**, then again (20 hawks and 10 Arcane Shots a fight, a use about every 6 seconds). A hawk dives for 108 plus 5% of your ranged attack power, then attacks for 18 seconds; only 2 can be out, and one every 9 seconds keeps both out nearly all fight.

**Aimed Shot** whenever it is ready: a 2-second cast on a 6-second cooldown, 23 casts a fight, 10% stronger with 2 points in **Barrage**. **Multi-Shot** shares that cooldown and is switched off for a single target ("Use Multi-Shot").

From 5 seconds in, every other cooldown as it comes ready: **Rapid Fire** (40% faster attacks for 15 seconds) once, your on-use trinket (the page's sets carry Blackhand's Breadth) and a Major Mana Potion. At 27 Beast Mastery points there is no **Bestial Wrath** to time, and **Intimidation** has no line: it only counts toward the points **Frenzy** needs.

The pet half: **Unleashed Fury** (+15% damage to the cat and the hawks), **Ferocity** (+10% crit to both), **Frenzy** (2 points: a 40% chance of 30% faster attacks for 8 seconds after each pet crit) and **Focused Fire** (+2% to you both while the cat is out). The cat takes a tenth of your attack power and your crit chance, and attacks and uses Claw on its own.
caveats: Full raid: every raid buff and debuff, phase-1 gear, 3-minute fights. The list has no mana guard: on the simulator's training dummy (your own buffs only), the raid's mana buffs alone (Mana Spring Totem, Mana Tide Totem, Greater Blessing of Wisdom, Judgement of Wisdom) add 18% to this build's damage.

Keep the cat alive with **Mend Pet**: Forever pets take no stat buffs from players. In the simulator a pet keeps the attack power it took from you when called until it is dismissed (its authors' reading of combat logs), so call it after your buffs are up.

The pet and the hawks are the simulator's models, unmeasured at 60: since 2026-11-19 a faster pet's swing hits for less, so its damage a second stays the same (fitted to one level-30 combat log), and the hawks' attacks after the dive, which the game files do not describe, are fitted to combat logs.
Track the boss's creature type: **Improved Tracking** (2 points here) adds 2% only against the tracked type; the simulator's boss is an Elemental.

Ranks: the list casts the trainer's top ranks, **Serpent Sting** rank 8 and **Aspect of the Hawk** rank 6 (ranks 9 and 7 are class books, not in Forever on the evidence there is; checked again when the raids open on 2026-12-09). For **Hunter's Mark** the simulator uses rank 3's +98 ranged attack power, as the client data it reads lists rank 4 lower; the beta tooltip (build 70753) reads rank 4 +143. Cast whichever rank your tooltip shows higher.

Moving: **Auto Shot** and **Aimed Shot** stop while you move; **Arcane Shot**, **Serpent Sting** and **Summon Hawk** are instant. Move right after an **Auto Shot** goes off, as the simulator's walk to its spot does ("Windup close", "Just shot").

The page's With a pet setup (22/29/0, also with **Summon Hawk**) runs another entry's list: the official turret file with our search's edits of 2026-11-20, which drop the turret file's hawk switch, add a **Summon Hawk** line above 60% mana and put a Major Mana Potion at the end. It plays like this page's list (20 hawks, 9 Arcane Shots, 23 Aimed Shots a fight) with a second Major Mana Potion: 905 DPS there, 905.6 on the official hawk file.
diverge: Two or more targets close together: **Multi-Shot** in place of **Aimed Shot** (it hits 3 targets). For a pack, **Volley**: a 6-second channel with no cooldown.
In the last few seconds, skip the **Serpent Sting** recast: its damage comes over 15 seconds.
Inside 8 yards your shots and **Auto Shot** stop: step back out. **Summon Hawk** has no minimum range, and the cat keeps attacking meanwhile.
Short on mana: let **Aimed Shot** go first. In this build's full-raid numbers it does about 1,160 damage for 310 mana, **Arcane Shot** 830 for 190, **Serpent Sting** 1,640 for 230.

leveling.plan: Beast-Marks levels like Beast Mastery without its two cooldowns: the cat tanks and you shoot from range. The split takes Marksmanship first (levels 10-30 and 32: **Lethal Attacks**, **Efficiency**, **Improved Stings**, **Careful Aim**, **Trueshot Aura**, **Rapid Killing** and **Rapid Recuperation**), **Improved Tracking** at 31, 33-35 and 60, and the pet talents (36-59: **Deadly Aspects**, **Focused Fire**, **Unleashed Fury**, **Ferocity**, **Bestial Discipline**).
why: Send the pet first, then **Hunter's Mark** and **Serpent Sting** while the mob is still healthy (the fight lab: above 30% and 40% of its health). The cat holds the mob until your threat passes 130% of its own. In the fight lab's removal runs at 60 (seconds a kill costs without the talent), **Unleashed Fury** (46-50) is worth about 1.0 second, **Efficiency** (15-19) 0.75 and **Ferocity** (51-55) 0.7: the build's most valuable talents, ahead of **Improved Stings** (20-22) and **Lethal Attacks** (10-14), about 0.5 each.

**Aimed Shot** (from level 20) is your only cooldown shot on a single mob, cast while the mob has more than 35% of its health: below that, **Auto Shot** and the pet finish the mob, which the tuned rules (2026-11-15) measured slightly faster. The rules never cast **Multi-Shot** (it shares the cooldown) or **Arcane Shot**: their mana is worth more as fewer drinks between pulls. This build has no **Summon Hawk** point anyway.

**Rapid Fire** at the start of a fight when it is ready: **Rapid Killing** (27 and 29) cuts its cooldown from 5 minutes to 3 and opens **Rapid Recuperation** (30, one point). After **Serpent Sting**, that lets a quarter of your mana regeneration continue while casting for 15 seconds (half after you spend a **Rapid Killing**). Until **Bestial Discipline** (57, one point), which gives the quarter all the time, it is the build's mana in a fight; at 60 the two overlap, and the removal runs measure **Rapid Recuperation** at nothing and **Bestial Discipline** at about 0.2 seconds.

**Auto Shot** with **Aimed Shot** and the sting is most of your own damage, the cat the rest, and **Auto Shot** cannot fire within 8 yards: step back out if the mob ends up beside you. **Mend Pet** when the pet drops below about a third.
**Trueshot Aura** (level 25) is a buff you cast in Forever: keep it on.
caveats: This build does not take **Bestial Wrath**, nor **Intimidation**, so the list leaves out the step that names them, and **Rapid Fire** with it: still press **Rapid Fire** at the start of a fight when it is ready.

**Endurance Training** (43-44), **Improved Revive Pet** (45) and **Spirit Bond** (59) measured nothing at 60 in the fight lab, where the pet rarely dies. The leveling filler pass of 2026-11-15 moved the other points that measured nothing (Pathfinding, a second **Spirit Bond**, **Rapid Recuperation**'s and **Bestial Discipline**'s second points) to **Bestial Swiftness** (56), **Mortal Shots** (58) and **Improved Tracking** (31 and 60). **Rapid Killing** measured almost nothing: its shot bonus after a kill is not in the fight lab.
**Improved Tracking** (levels 33-35, 3 points) adds 1% a point, and only against the creature type you are tracking: switch tracking to what you are killing.

The lab drinks below 15% of your mana (the tuned rules of 2026-11-15: fewer stops measured slightly faster) and eats below 65% of your health. Whenever you sit down to drink or eat, do both while the other bar is not full: it costs no extra time (the tuned rules of 2026-11-17). A mob that turns on you: **Feign Death** sends it back to the pet; while it is on cooldown, **Mongoose Bite**, **Raptor Strike** and **Wing Clip** hold it until the pet's Growl takes it back.

Buy the new ranks: in the beta client (build 70753) the top ranks are the strongest. **Aspect of the Hawk** rank 7 gives +120 ranged attack power (rank 6 +110), **Hunter's Mark** rank 4 +143 (rank 3 +98) and **Trueshot Aura** rank 5 +100 (rank 4 +75). Cast the highest rank you know; the fight lab does.
**Auto Shot** keeps firing while you cast **Aimed Shot**, but after you step back it waits until you have stood still for half a second (Blizzard's 16 Oct notes), so don't shuffle between shots.
diverge: Several mobs: **Multi-Shot** and **Volley** (no cooldown in Forever) instead of single-target shots.
If the pet dies, finish the mob in melee or **Feign Death**, and revive it before the next pull. When a mob is nearly dead, stop spending mana and let **Auto Shot** and the pet finish it.

leveling.plan: The split melee build plays the melee Survival list: walk in behind the pet, trap at your feet and fight beside it. Its Marksmanship points buy crit and attack power (**Lethal Attacks**, **Careful Aim**), and **Survivalist's Discipline** brings the trap back sooner.
why: **Serpent Sting** as the mob runs in, from range, then walk in behind the pet: the fight lab's tuned rules (2026-11-03) cast it while the mob has more than 40% of its health, and never cast **Hunter's Mark** for a melee hunter.
**Immolation Trap** at your feet beside the mob, while it has more than 40% of its health (the burn lasts 15 seconds). **Survivalist's Discipline** cuts its cooldown from 30 to 18 seconds.

**Raptor Strike** once the mob is below 20% of its health (it replaces your next main-hand swing and costs no global cooldown). **Lacerate** only while the mob has more than half its health and you have 80% of your mana or more.

**Mongoose Bite** when it lights up after you dodge. **Expose Prey** would also light it up from your hits on a marked mob, but the tuned rules never cast **Hunter's Mark**. **Counterattack** after you parry; **Deflection** raises your parry.

**Deterrence** below 40% health while the mob has more than 30% of its health: +25% dodge and parry for 10 seconds, every 3 minutes with **Survivalist's Discipline**, and those dodges and parries light up **Mongoose Bite** and **Counterattack**.

Between fights the lab drinks below 35% of your mana and eats below 65% of your health: the tuned rules change neither. Whenever you sit down to drink or eat, do both while the other bar is not full: it costs no extra time (the tuned rules of 2026-11-17).
caveats: The tuned rules cast **Raptor Strike** and **Strider Kick** only once the mob is below 20% of its health, and **Lacerate** only above half its health with 80% of your mana. The project counts a melee hunter's damage as swings, strikes, bleeds and the pet (at least half at 60).
**Aspect of the Monkey** until level 30, then **Aspect of the Beast** for its melee attack power; **Deadly Aspects** adds its swing-speed chance to **Aspect of the Beast**.
**Improved Tracking** (levels 10-14) adds damage only against the creature type you are tracking: keep tracking set to what you are killing.

Buy the new ranks: in the beta client (build 70753) the top ranks are the strongest. **Aspect of the Beast** rank 4 gives +110 melee attack power at 60 (rank 3 +90); the other ranks of the spells you press only add damage. Cast the highest rank you know; the fight lab does.
diverge: Two or more mobs: **Explosive Trap** instead of **Immolation Trap**; it hits everything within 10 yards and shares the fire-trap cooldown.
If the pet dies, **Deterrence** and finish the mob, or **Feign Death** if it is going badly; revive the pet before the next pull.

raid.plan: Beast-Survival plays the Survival melee list with no pet out: **Lone Wolf** adds 20% to everything you do while no pet is out, and the simulator counts hawks as guardians, not pets, so **Summon Hawk** keeps two hawks on the boss most of the fight without turning it off. This is the official simulator's own melee rotation (since 2026-11-20, when it beat ours by 2.2% on this build). In a 3-minute raid fight: **Wing Clip** 37 casts, **Raptor Strike** 24, **Summon Hawk** 22, **Strider Kick** 20, **Mongoose Bite** 20, **Serpent Sting** 9, **Immolation Trap** 7; your white swings 29% of the damage, the hawks 15% (swings 11%, dives 4%), **Serpent Sting** 9%, Windfury Totem's extra swings 9%, **Raptor Strike** 8%, **Mongoose Bite** 8%, **Immolation Trap** 7%, **Strider Kick** 7%.
why: Before the pull: **Dismiss Pet** (a 5-second cast), then **Hunter's Mark** and **Aspect of the Beast** (+110 melee attack power; with **Deadly Aspects** each melee auto attack has a 10% chance to speed your swings by 30% for 12 seconds). The simulator walks you in from 25 yards, casting **Serpent Sting**, **Arcane Shot** and **Multi-Shot** on the way. From 5 seconds in the other cooldowns go as they come ready: **Rapid Fire** (40% faster melee attacks too, for 15 seconds) once, on-use trinkets and a Major Mana Potion.
**Raptor Strike** first: it replaces your next main-hand swing and costs no global cooldown, so queue it whenever its 6-second cooldown ends.

**Hunter's Mark** whenever it is missing: with **Expose Prey**, each of your hits on a marked target has a 10% chance to light up **Mongoose Bite** for 10 seconds, and in a raid the boss hits your tank, so your own dodges, the bite's other trigger, rarely come. Bite at once: weapon damage plus 57 on a 5-second cooldown.

**Strider Kick** on cooldown (full weapon damage, 8 seconds), and its 3 seconds of 30% speed are your window for **Serpent Sting**: with the sting off the boss and more than 30% mana, run out past your shots' 8-yard minimum range (the simulator goes to about 13 yards), sting, shoot **Arcane Shot** and **Multi-Shot** if they are ready, and walk back in, pausing for an **Auto Shot** when one is due.
**Immolation Trap** whenever it is ready, set in melee at the boss: 690 Fire damage over 15 seconds, 30% more with **Clever Traps**, every 24 seconds with 1 point in **Survivalist's Discipline**.

**Summon Hawk** next: a dive for 108 plus 5% of your ranged attack power, then a hawk that attacks for 18 seconds, two at a time, 15% harder with **Unleashed Fury**. **Endurance Training** does nothing without a pet; its 5 points only open **Unleashed Fury**'s row.
**Wing Clip** fills every global cooldown left: its own hit is 50 damage, but each hit on your marked target is another 10% chance at **Mongoose Bite**.
caveats: Full raid: every raid buff and debuff, phase-1 gear, 3-minute fights. Windfury Totem's extra swings are 9% of your damage: you need a shaman's totem in your group. There it does 864 DPS, against 915 for the Survival page's build with a Raptor and 836 for Melee Survival with **Lone Wolf**, all on this rotation.

Mana: no **Resourcefulness** or **Efficiency**, and each hawk costs 190 mana. On the simulator's training dummy (your own buffs only), the raid's mana buffs alone (Mana Spring Totem, Mana Tide Totem, Greater Blessing of Wisdom, Judgement of Wisdom) add 43% to its damage, and there it does 303 DPS against 364 for the Survival page's build. Without Blessing of Wisdom or Mana Spring Totem, play Survival.
The build rests on the simulator's reading that a hawk is a guardian, not a pet: if the game counts hawks as pets, **Lone Wolf** turns off while they are out. Check it at launch.
The class page says **Expose Prey** needs your own **Hunter's Mark**; the simulator accepts any hunter's. With several hunters, make sure the mark on the boss is yours.
Traps in combat are the simulator's assumption, still to check in game: a trap lies where you stand and springs on the boss beside you, so the list sets it only in melee.

Track the boss's creature type: **Improved Tracking** adds 5% only against the tracked type. Ranks: **Serpent Sting** rank 8 (rank 9 is a class book, not in Forever on the evidence there is) and **Aspect of the Beast** rank 4.
diverge: Adds around you: **Multi-Shot** on the way in hits 3 targets, and for a pack set **Explosive Trap** instead of **Immolation Trap** (everything within 10 yards). The official list never casts it, and the simulator gives all traps one cooldown, so it is one or the other.
Pulled off the boss by a mechanic: **Summon Hawk** reaches 35 yards, so keep the hawks coming, and make **Strider Kick** your last hit before you run (30% movement speed for 3 seconds).

Short on mana: the list already skips the **Serpent Sting** trips below 30%; let **Wing Clip** go next, about 80 damage for 80 mana in this build's full-raid numbers, the least for its mana of anything you press.
If you pull threat, **Feign Death** (30-second cooldown).

leveling.plan: Beast-Survival levels on **Immolation Trap** and a strong pet: the cat tanks and hits hard, you walk in behind it, drop a trap at your feet and fight beside it with **Raptor Strike** and your white swings. Survival comes first (levels 10-34), then **Lethal Attacks** (35-37) and the pet (38-60).
why: **Immolation Trap** is the heart of the build: **Clever Traps** (levels 23-24) adds to it, **Survival Tactics** (29) helps it hit, and **Survivalist's Discipline** (33-34) brings it back every 18 seconds. In the fight lab's removal runs at 60 (seconds a kill costs without the talent), **Resourcefulness** (levels 30 and 32: cheaper traps and strikes) is worth about 2.0 seconds and **Survivalist's Discipline** 1.1, the build's most valuable talents; **Bestial Discipline** and **Unleashed Fury**, about 0.6 each, and **Clever Traps**, 0.55, come next.
Set the trap at your feet beside the mob (traps work in combat in Forever but land where you stand), only while the mob has more than 40% of its health (the burn lasts 15 seconds).

**Serpent Sting** as the mob runs in, from range (more than 8 yards away, mob above 40% of its health), then walk in behind the pet. **Raptor Strike** only once the mob is below 20% of its health: the tuned rules (2026-11-03) hold it for the finish (it replaces your next main-hand swing and costs no global cooldown). **Mongoose Bite** lights up only after you dodge, which is rare while the pet holds the mob: the fight lab casts it almost never (none at 60). **Lacerate** (from level 30) only while the mob has more than half its health and you have 80% of your mana or more.

From level 35 the points go to **Lethal Attacks** (35-37, after a first point at 31) and then Beast Mastery: **Deadly Aspects** (38-42) for your swings, then the pet: **Focused Fire** (43-44), **Endurance Training** (45-47), **Unleashed Fury** (48-52), **Ferocity** (53-57) and **Bestial Discipline** (58-59); the fifth **Predator's Edge** point comes at 60. The cat's swings and Claw are a large part of the damage at 60: send it first and let it hold the mob.

The tuned rules never cast **Hunter's Mark**, so the build takes no **Expose Prey**, which lights up **Mongoose Bite** only from hits on a marked mob: the leveling filler pass of 2026-11-15 moved that point to **Lethal Attacks** (31), 0.4% faster per kill. **Aspect of the Monkey** until level 30, then **Aspect of the Beast**. Between fights the lab drinks below 35% of your mana and eats below 65% of your health. Whenever you sit down to drink or eat, do both while the other bar is not full: it costs no extra time (the tuned rules of 2026-11-17).
caveats: This build takes no **Strider Kick**, nor **Counterattack**, nor **Deterrence**: the list above leaves their lines out. Between traps your global cooldown is mostly free, and white swings and the pet do most of the damage.

The list is shared with Survival: the tuned rules hold **Raptor Strike** (this build lacks **Strider Kick**) for the last 20% of the mob's health. The project counts a melee hunter's damage as swings, strikes, bleeds and the pet (at least half at 60; this build reaches 60%).
**Savage Strikes** (15-16), **Survivalist** (17-18) and **Entrapment** (19) measured almost nothing at 60 in the fight lab: they fill the tree's first rows.
**Improved Tracking** (levels 10-14) adds 1% a point, and only against the creature type you are tracking: switch tracking to what you are killing.

Buy the new ranks: in the beta client (build 70753) the top ranks are the strongest. **Aspect of the Beast** rank 4 gives +110 melee attack power at 60 (rank 3 +90); the other ranks of the spells you press only add damage. Cast the highest rank you know; the fight lab does.
diverge: Two or more mobs: **Explosive Trap** instead of **Immolation Trap**; it hits everything within 10 yards and shares the fire-trap cooldown.
Low on health: **Mend Pet** keeps your tank up, and **Feign Death** drops the mob back on the pet if it turns on you.
